item.title: Turn your handwriting into a font for Android, Windows, or MacOS
item.description: Handwriting has personality. Get to know someone well enough and their handwriting will remind you of them, because we all form letters just a bit differently. Our devices, for the most part, lack that kind of personality.
item.dc:creator: Justin Pot, Fast Company

item.title: Inside the Trump administration’s $2 billion push to build the world’s first useful quantum computer
item.description: The White House Quantum Summit brought together dozens of quantum policy officials and industry leaders last month, representing a rare glimmer of bipartisanship as the U.S. hustles to become the first nation to build a fault-tolerant quantum computer.
item.dc:creator: Inc., Fast Company

item.title: Workers are worried AI will expose they don't know how to do their jobs properly
item.description: Workers are becoming aware of gaps and limitations in their own abilities thanks to their use of AI, and they’re concerned they may be considered replaceable
item.dc:creator: Christian Cawley, TechRadar

item.title: What we lose when every engineer can do everything
item.description: Four months ago, a front-end engineer on my team looking to make upgrades to a product or feature would have filed a ticket and waited for the infrastructure group to unblock them. They might have lost a day, sometimes a week. Today, that same engineer makes changes themselves.
item.dc:creator: Info World

item.title: Samsung offers future AI memory roadmap
item.description: Samsung Electronics has unveiled a trio of next-generation memory technologies aimed at overcoming the performance, power and capacity limitations facing artificial intelligence infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Network World

item.title: Polish data center plans to send its waste heat to the neighbors
item.description: As Europe swelters in a heatwave, residents probably don’t want to hear about ways to make their homes even hotter, but that’s what Polish property developer Citylink is talking about, with plans to dump waste heat from a new data center in Wrocław into the municipal district heating network.
item.dc:creator: Computer World

item.title: Cloudflare wants to provide the operating system for the AI-first enterprise
item.description: Traditional operating systems (OS) were built to manage hardware, files, apps, and users on a device, but Cloudflare says the agentic AI era requires a whole new format.
item.dc:creator: Computer World

item.title: SpaceX shares rise even as company insiders get a chance to sell for the first time
item.description: Stock in Elon Musk’s space company rose Thursday even after many SpaceX insiders were freed up to sell for the first time.
item.dc:creator: Bernard Condon, Associated Press, KPRC 2

item.title: OpenAI’s ‘Rotten to the core’ defense is its weakest play yet
item.description: Ancient Greek sophist Protagoras famously said, “There are two sides to every question.” But OpenAI’s latest attempt at reality distortion seems determined to narrow this dispute to just one.
item.dc:creator: Computer World

item.title: Testing is underway on vaccines to intercept brewing colon cancer before it takes root
item.description: Scientists are creating a new kind of vaccine that teaches the immune system to intercept a type of brewing colon cancer before it turns into a full-fledged tumor.
item.dc:creator: Lauran Neergaard, Associated Press, Local 4

item.title: Climate change created conditions for Canada fires, scientists say, as Trump blames mismanagement
item.description: A new study calculates that human-caused climate change doubled the likelihood of the tinderbox weather conditions that sparked Canada’s massive summer wildfires.
item.dc:creator: Seth Borenstein, Associated Press, KPRC 2

item.title: Enterprise passkey security under threat from malware
item.description: Given the widespread enterprise adoption of passkeys to replace passwords, a Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 report disclosing ways attackers are getting around passkey protections is concerning, analysts say, but they stress that the demonstrated attacks can only happen after a successful intrusion.
item.dc:creator: Computer World

item.title: Cybertrucks are replacing NASA’s military escape vehicles at SpaceX launches
item.description: Cybertrucks will soon make an appearance at NASA space launches. At a recent news conference in advance of a launch to the International Space Station, NASA officials said the space agency will use the iconoclastic Tesla electric pickup trucks as backup emergency escape vehicles.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Heilweil, Fast Company

item.title: Microsoft moves to limit AI use by its employees
item.description: Until recently, it was common for companies and organizations to engage in “tokenmaxxing” — that is, maximizing their use of AI. But with AI costs going up, companies are now looking to save money, a trend underscored by a recent Microsoft decision to limit AI use by its employees.
item.dc:creator: Computer World

item.title: Fuego volcano activity that triggered evacuations in Guatemala is decreasing, but risks remain
item.description: Guatemalan authorities say activity at the Fuego volcano is gradually decreasing after it began two days ago.
item.dc:creator: Sonia Pérez D., Associated Press, KPRC 2

item.title: AWS updates DynamoDB with native vector search to ease AI application development
item.description: AWS is finally adding native vector search to its managed NoSQL database DynamoDB, which is typically used to store high-volume operational and transactional data.
item.dc:creator: Info World

item.title: 2026 network outage report and internet health check
item.description: ThousandEyes, a Cisco company, monitors how ISPs, cloud providers and conferencing services are handling any performance challenges and provides Network World with a weekly roundup of events that impact service delivery.
item.dc:creator: Network World

item.title: The scam text test: Spot danger before you tap
item.description: A simple six-step scam text test helps you spot phishing messages about fake deliveries, toll notices and bank alerts before you click or share anything.
item.dc:creator: Fox News

item.title: AWS’s Kiro Crew aims to turn AI coding agents into autonomous engineering teams
item.description: AWS on Tuesday released Kiro Crew, an open-source orchestration platform designed to help enterprises move beyond interactive AI coding assistants toward long-running, autonomous engineering workflows that span repositories, developer tools, and multiple work sessions.
item.dc:creator: Info World
